Inspired by the grace and symmetry of classical realism,
my works explores an irresistible alchemy of sensuality and sentiment,
a form of beauty that is sometimes distorted by our demons,
and other times enchanted by all that’s pure within our souls.
The three bodies of work that have evolved from this figurative heritage
are what I believe to be timeless commentaries on our human condition

attributes.text: “Inspired by the grace and symmetry of classical realism, my work explores an irresistible alchemy of sensuality and sentiment — a form of beauty sometimes distorted by our demons, and other times enchanted by all that is pure within our souls.”
Blake William Ward born in Yellowknife, Northwest Territories, Canada, on June 3, 1956, and raised in Edmonton.

Holding to his appreciation of the human figure, Ward remains true to the representational quality and realistic proportions of traditional sculpture while continually finding new ways to comment on the human condition.
Exhibitions of his work have travelled across three continents North America, Europe and Asia from Monte-Carlo and Paris to Singapore, Hong Kong and India.
Receives an Honours Degree in Fine Art from the University of Alberta.
Moves to Paris to study figurative sculpture under Cyril Heck.
Relocates to Monaco and opens his Monte-Carlo studio, close to his foundry and marble quarry.
